unexpressed.scope: 2026-09-09: this is no longer a single-site observation, and it is the smallest of the route differences. A scan of all twelve local ROMs counts the inline form 0 times in every TBS ROM and 2067-2081 times in every TLA ROM across r0 through r13, while veneer calls run 916-924 per TBS ROM against 23 per TLA ROM, and every remaining TLA veneer caller lies in code inherited verbatim from the TBS build or in the shared audio engine. TBS owner 080bbb0c reaches the same source construct at offset 0082, BATTLE_COPY_UNIT through a constant IWRAM address, via an R_ARM_THM_CALL against _call_via_r3, so the construct corresponds and only its lowering differs. Two further whole-image measurements reframe this: TLA returns from framed functions through pop {..., pc}, which agscc emits only when TARGET_INTERWORK is clear, so TLA game code was compiled without -mthumb-interwork and tools/alchemy/src/compiler/routing.rs sets that flag wrongly for TLA today; and TLA synthesizes non-shiftable Thumb constants inline, 4134-4148 sites per TLA ROM against 9-12 per TBS ROM and 86 inside this owner, where the pinned compilers pool them, which costs this candidate 106 bytes and is the dominant cause of the pool-placement divergence previously attributed to branch-range tension. Everything else fingerprints as the same GCC 2.96 family and the same -fcall-used-r4 ABI as TBS. All three measurements and their methods are recorded in games/tla/recon/cross-edition.json under indirect_call_lowering. The blocker is the TLA build route, not this owner's source, and it gates TLA game-code recovery generally; only Pascal may establish a TLA route or output transformation, and this dossier authorizes neither. The call site is still only four bytes of 8300 and is size-neutral: it explains why exactness is unreachable, not why the candidate stands at 3971 differing halfwords.
